@graph.name: Do we need a Conexiom alternative for spoken restaurant orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Conexiom goes on reading the POs customers email you, and none of its rules change. VoiceOrder Solutions is for the restaurants that call: the chef names each item aloud in our app, sees each one matched to a product on the guide for that kitchen, and reviews it all before it goes to you.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Conexiom?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one thing: getting a restaurant that still calls to send its order already matched to your catalog. Reading POs, invoices and other paperwork in whatever layout it arrives is Conexiom's work, so we work next to it and are not a Conexiom alternative.

@graph.name: Conexiom reads text messages. Why not ask chefs to text?

acceptedAnswer.text: A text comes in the chef's own shorthand, such as "romaine, two", so Relay still has to work out which of your products it means. In our app, each spoken item is matched to the restaurant's own guide, and the chef sees which of your products was picked before sending.

@graph.name: Does it connect to Conexiom, and do we still key orders in by hand?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not directly. They come from two different companies, no link joins them as standard, and each company looks after its own software only. Over EDI or our API, the chef's order can go into your ERP and nobody types it again, if your ERP is set up for it; we check that in a demo. By email, you get it as an attachment. Whether your Conexiom setup can read that file is something to ask Conexiom: we have built nothing for it and make no promise. If it cannot, one of your people keys it in from the list the chef already checked, with no call to take, write down and read back. Your accounts, your stock and your invoices still live in your ERP. We hold the restaurant guides, the prices on them, and copies of what chefs send through the app.

@graph.name: Conexiom maps each customer's format. What does adding a restaurant take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Conexiom's FAQ describes mapping each customer's PO format with your customer service team, usually rolling out to a handful of customers first. A new restaurant needs no mapping, because there is no customer format to learn: the guide starts from what you already sell that restaurant, and the chef's spoken order is matched to it.

@graph.name: How long until we are live, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours, with no change made in Conexiom. You send us the items each account usually orders, most often as a spreadsheet export, and we load them into our admin and set up every account. Once the restaurants have the app on their phones, most of them order the same day. Conexiom sells by subscription and quotes each business, with no price on its site, and we quote per distributor too. A Conexiom replacement would mean rebuilding every customer's mapping and rules in another reader, a separate job from putting an app in front of the chefs still calling you.

@graph.name: Does the app get every item right?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. It turns the chef's words into items from the guide, and a chef can overlook a wrong one or change their mind once it is sent. The difference is that the person who decided the order reads it on screen before it goes, and each item the app matches comes from that kitchen's guide.

@graph.name: Where do the Conexiom details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From conexiom.com, as we read it on 9 November 2026: the homepage, the Platform, Relay, Headless Platform and Solutions pages, its FAQ and About pages, and its glossary pages on line item capture, price checks and unit conversion. Searching the web that day turned up no voice or call ordering tool for Conexiom. If any of it has moved on, write to us and we will correct the page.
